messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a weird case in the console: composite endpoint /v2/chat shows p95 lower than p50 for the 'mobile' slice after the routing-policy rollforward.
cheng: huh, can you paste the screenshot or numbers?
maya: p50 240ms, p95 180ms, p99 320ms. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.internal/short/snap123.png
sam: that's... impossible for a single distribution. Most likely mixing sample origins. Did the routing change start tagging origins differently? @cheng any recent route-tag PRs? :thinking_face:
cheng: I merged a tiny change to add fallback-route attribution but it only touched the gateway tag. Could be a merge where the dashboard rollup is blending server vs gateway samples incorrectly.
rajesh: Another possibility: the console p-percentiles toggle ("derive from: endpoint | route | backend") falls back to the route-level t-digest when counts are low. If p50 was computed on raw samples and p95 from cached tdigest merges we can get inversion when they come from different populations.
maya: omg that would explain it. We should show provenance inline.
sam: agreed. Short-term: add a badge in the legend that says "percentile source: tdigest(route) / raw(endpoint)". Long-term: unify derivation or expose API option.
rajesh: API idea: add query param `percentile_source` with allowed values `auto|raw|tdigest` and `origin_tag` to force which sample origin to include. Example:

```
GET /api/v1/metrics/percentiles?endpoint=/v2/chat&slice=mobile&percentile=95&percentile_source=raw
```

Will return percentiles derived only from raw sample stream (no tdigest rollups).
cheng: that API is fine but careful: raw queries are expensive and can blow up the console latency/backend costs. Need guardrails (sample cap, fallback to tdigest after X samples).
sam: what if we add `preview=true` and a sample_limit param so UI can request a cheap subset, and we show a warning.
console-ux: @sam @rajesh that matches our UX rationale — we want transparency but not slow dashboards. UX proposal: show a small breakout panel when you hover a percentile that shows: sample_count, derivation_method, sample_origin, and a "Recompute from raw" button (with a spinner and cost warning).
maya: love that. Can we also flag requests that include retries? Best to be explicit about whether retries are included in the sample origin.
rajesh: yes add `include_retries=true|false` to the API and propagate to tdigest ingestion tags.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-service v2.14.3 — includes metric tag propagation for `sample_origin` (deployed to prod-canary)
sam: ok next steps: (1) cheng, add guardrail limits to raw-percentile endpoint; (2) raresh/telemetry, ensure ingestion tags include `sample_origin` and `include_retries`; (3) console-ux, mockup hover panel; (4) maya, check a few other composite endpoints for PCTL inversion and collect examples.
cheng: I'll open a PR for the guardrails and add unit tests for mixed-origin merges.
rajesh: I'll follow up with telemetry healthcheck for tdigest merges.
maya: thanks everyone. I'll drop a short note in #product about the UX change so PMs don't freak when numbers move. :thumbsup:
